_meta.zeroIsAClaim: A rule returning ZERO findings on the live tree is a claim requiring evidence, not a pass (Bean-locked, 2026-08-03, after coordinator review caught rule 01 counting <InspectorControls> elements instead of panels and silently missing 42+ real unrouted blocks — including hero, the specific block flagged as unusable). Whoever adds a rule MUST: (1) state its expected population BEFORE trusting a live run, using a method independent of the rule's own code — a second script in a different style, a manual grep, or a hand count; (2) if the rule returns 0 or a suspiciously round/small number, treat that as a red flag and re-derive the condition from what the checklist item actually requires, not from what was easy to detect in one file; (3) record the comparison (expected vs actual) somewhere reviewable before setting the rule's advisoryReason. All three shipped rules here (01/18/20) were cross-checked this way on 2026-08-03: 01 measured 65 (was silently 0 under the first, wrong condition), 18 measured 15 (was 12 before a shared-component blind spot — MediaPicker.js — was found and fixed), 20 measured 23 (was 43 before a wrong exclusion mechanism — filename prefix instead of the pattern's own 'Post Types:' header — was found and fixed).

A row whose SOLE declared state is a real, admitted, non-`normal` state (golden-controls.json _meta.stateVocabulary.real: hover / current / scrolled) no longer counts as below the state floor. It is not a row that forgot its hover; it IS a state. 18 rows, 13 blocks, all below-min-states, ZERO net-new, verified by key-set diff normalised on block+kind+rowKey -- never the raw key, which embeds a line number and mis-reported 45 removed / 26 added on the first attempt purely because a concurrent track's edits to post-grid/testimonial shifted lines. Baselines captured BACK-TO-BACK with only these two files swapped, so the delta isolates the rule change from that concurrent work. THREE LEGITIMATE SHAPES, enumerated not inferred: (1) the HOVER HALF of a split control -- sgs/testimonial's row is labelled 'Border colour (hover)' and paints borderColourHover, while the RESTING half borderColour is owned by SgsBorderControl, a component this rule cannot see. Adding a 'normal' state there would give the colour panel write-access to an attribute another control already owns, so the 'fix' would be the duplicate-writer defect this project bans; (2) a colour for a HOVER-ONLY FEATURE -- info-box/testimonial shadowHover rows are gated behind the shadowHover toggle and colour a shadow that exists only on hover; (3) a STATE-SCOPED row -- sgs/tabs' panel-bg and panel-border paint the CURRENT panel, the only state a panel has. ⛔ THIS DOES NOT WEAKEN THE 2-STATE FLOOR (states.minimumMeans, Bean 2026-08-19). TWO FIXTURES, paired: sole-declared-state-row (mustNotFlag) and the identical-but-for-the-state-key sole-unknown-state-row (mustFlag), proving the exemption matches without over-matching -- a typo must not buy silent exemption or the floor stops meaning anything. Advisory FIRST per E6 point 9 — never promote on the run that introduces the rule. ⚠ READ THE PREDICTION AND ITS FALSIFICATION TOGETHER — the prediction was WRONG and the way it was wrong is the point. PREDICTED 1, MEASURED 3. The prediction (declared before the first live run per _meta.zeroIsAClaim) came from a shell census over src/blocks/*/block.json + render.php: 28 blocks declare contentWidth (D540's own 33 minus the 5 it deleted) and 'all 28 route through SGS_Container_Wrapper'. Two independent errors sat in that sentence. (a) D540's own conclusion that wrapper-routing implies a band is FALSE: three call sites override the guard via $opts['wrap_inner'] (class-sgs-container-wrapper.php:81,112) — physics-canvas/render.php:97 forces it TRUE (clean); hero/render.php:1065-1066 suppresses it for split but bands the content with centred padding-inline on the grid (:326-341), which is a REAL band and the correct mechanism there, since a grid item is sized by its track and a max-width on the column would be an inert lever (Bean-ruled 2026-08-10, correcting an earlier draft of this rule that WOULD have flagged hero); product-card/render.php:313 suppresses it unconditionally in the $base_opts every branch shares and reads contentWidth nowhere in code (only a docblock at :21), so the wrapper writes band CSS to a selector that never renders. (b) The census itself was wrong: it grepped for the string 'SGS_Container_Wrapper' and MATCHED COMMENTS. sgs/info-box and sgs/option-picker both DROPPED the wrapper under D294 and mention it only in prose explaining that they dropped it — so both were counted as wrapper-routed while actually rendering block-private, each emitting `width:` from contentWidth and `max-width:` from maxWidth onto the SAME root selector (info-box/render.php:299-304, option-picker/render.php:347-352). That is verbatim the shape D540 described and deleted from five blocks. Same 'a comment is not a call' trap this rule's own header warns about for the render side, committed on the census side by the person writing it. MEASURED THEREFORE 3: product-card (inert), info-box, option-picker. REMEDIES DIFFER BY EVIDENCE, per Bean 2026-08-10: product-card's contentWidth DELETED (inert; 0 theme patterns and 0 canary posts set it); info-box and option-picker RENAMED contentWidth -> width, keeping behaviour byte-identical, because D540's own text says a block that genuinely wants a fixed width says `width` and these two demonstrably do — info-box is live on two published canary pages at 900px and 480px, so deletion would have changed real pages, which is exactly why the theme+canary evidence was gathered before choosing. Post-remedy live run: 0 FLAGGED. The rule is proven able to FAIL against real code, not fixtures alone: contentWidth was temporarily restored to sgs/quote, the run reported 1 finding naming it, and the revert was confirmed on disk (0 occurrences, empty git diff) before the 0 was trusted. openBacklog 0 is therefore a measured zero on a rule that has demonstrably flagged live code three times.

rules.advisoryReason: NEW 2026-08-18. Spec 35 F.1: a composite's selectors.typography must target its own ROOT, never a child's dead BEM class. Guards the THIRD defect layer (declared / rendered / CONSUMED) that no other rule checks: a native typography control can exist, render, and save a value while its generated CSS never reaches the painted element. WORKED EXAMPLE: sgs/hero's 7 declared native typography controls are silent no-ops because selectors.typography targets .sgs-hero__headline, which edit.js sets only as an InnerBlocks TEMPLATE child's className — the generated scoped rule sits at (0,2,0) and cannot beat that child block's own inline typography at (1,0,0,0), this framework's HC2 rule. A NAIVE TEXT SEARCH CANNOT SEE THIS, proven live: it returned 2 false positives (sgs/modal, sgs/social-icons — the WP-core-generated wp-block-sgs-* root class, legitimately absent from source) and MISSED hero entirely, because .sgs-hero__headline IS present in hero's files, just never as a DOM class attribute. The rule instead resolves the effective selector, extracts the class token, and classifies via AST (InnerBlocks-template ownership) plus a DOM-emission scan excluding this codebase's CSS-selector-building idiom (_sel / 'selector' / wp_style_engine). A REAL ENGINE BUG WAS FOUND AND FIXED DURING THE BUILD, and it matters beyond this rule: comparing AST line numbers against ctx.cache.strippedText() line numbers is WRONG, because strippedText() blanks a multi-line comment's entire character range INCLUDING its newlines, collapsing them and shifting every subsequent line number — that silently produced ZERO findings on hero, the one block this rule exists to catch. Character OFFSETS (node.start/node.end) stay aligned between raw and stripped text; line numbers do not. strippedText() also strips only /* */ in PHP and never //, so the rule carries its own quote-aware // stripper.
